# YAML and Kubernetes

Full rules, evidence and examples: `common/languages/yaml-kubernetes.md`.

- K8S-01 prefer: In Flux app repos, lay out an app as `<scope>/<group>/<app>/{kustomization.yaml, namespace.yaml, app/, extensions/}`: `app/` holds `ks.yaml`, `kustomization.yaml`, `kustomizeconfig.yaml`, `values.yaml` and `templates/{release,repository}.yaml`; `extensions/` holds its Flux `ks.yaml` and all non-Helm manifests. Shared apps live in `common/<group>/<app>`, site-specific in `sites/<site>/<group>/<app>`.
- K8S-02 must: Name manifest files `<kind>-<name>.yaml` in lowercase kebab-case with the `.yaml` extension. Exception: a file may bundle the tightly coupled resources of one app and carry the app name when the folder context makes the kinds clear (`external-services/app/templates/paseo.yaml`).
  Good: `external-secret-mealie-db.yaml`, `postgresql-backup.yaml`; `paseo.yaml` bundling the Service, EndpointSlice, ListenerSet, HTTPRoute and TrafficPolicy of one external service.
  Bad: `Secret_Mealie.yml`
- K8S-03 prefer: Define each Flux `Kustomization` with `name: &application <app>`, pass `APPLICATION: *application` and the namespace through `postBuild.substitute`, and set `interval: 10m`, `retryInterval: 2m`, `prune: true`, `wait: false`; name the extension kustomization `<app>-extensions`.
- K8S-04 prefer: Deploy Helm charts as an `OCIRepository` plus a `HelmRelease` with `chartRef` and values in a ConfigMap via `valuesFrom`; set `maxHistory: 3`, `install.strategy: RetryOnFailure`, `upgrade.remediation.retries: -1` and `rollback.recreate: true`.
- K8S-05 prefer: Use the bjw-s `app-template` for apps without a good upstream chart and key everything by app name; write image `repository`, `pullPolicy: IfNotPresent` and `tag` as separate keys and leave a blank line between `image`, `envFrom`, `env`, `resources` and `probes`.
- K8S-06 prefer: Set `requests.cpu`, `requests.memory` and `limits.memory` on every container, derive values from measured recommendations (KRR), and set no CPU limit unless a measured need exists.
- K8S-07 lean: Define probes once with an anchor (`liveness: &server_probes`), reuse it for readiness, use `custom: true` with explicit `httpGet`, and disable `startup` unless needed.
- K8S-08 must: Protect stateful resources of new apps from Git deletion: namespaces and databases carry `kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/prune: disabled` with a one-line guardrail comment, and PVCs set `retain: true` with a reason; add it to older apps when you touch them.
  Good: a new database namespace with `kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/prune: disabled` and a one-line comment saying why.
  Bad: a new stateful app whose namespace or PVC can be pruned by Flux.
- K8S-09 prefer: Give each app database a CloudNativePG `Cluster` named `<app>-postgresql` with explicit `resources`, `stopDelay: 300`, a backup and objectstore pair, a credentials ExternalSecret and a `# renovate:` comment above `imageName`; keep a commented-out `initdb` block beside the active `recovery` block as a deliberate switch, not dead code (PRIN-17).
- K8S-10 prefer: Create one `ExternalSecret` (the cluster's current API version, store `vault-auth`) per consumer secret and spell out `conversionStrategy: Default`, `decodingStrategy: None`, `key` and `property`; use SOPS only for bootstrap (`secret-*.enc.yaml`).
- K8S-11 prefer: Expose apps through Gateway API (`ListenerSet`, `HTTPRoute`) with external-dns and cert-manager annotations fed by Flux variables; cert-manager issues the certificate through the `ListenerSet` annotation, not a separate `Certificate`. Set the Gatus enabled annotation on routes that Helm values define; on a hand-written `HTTPRoute` manifest add it only when the app should be probed.
- K8S-12 prefer: Define per-site values that more than one manifest uses once in `cluster-configuration.yaml` as SCREAMING_SNAKE variables grouped under lowercase comment headers; a value used by one manifest may stay a literal there (an exception to PRIN-25). The owner usually adds the entries by hand: propose a new variable instead of editing the file unprompted.
- K8S-13 prefer: Kubernetes: write section headers in flat config maps as lowercase noun phrases; other comments follow PRIN-15.

Avoid (AI-Era Artifacts):

- AI-era artifacts: commented-out options kept as leftovers (`# ipFamilyPolicy: PreferDualStack` x5); only deliberate switches stay.
- Emoji or box-drawing in validation script output.
- Vague repeated commit subjects for tuning runs (see COMMIT-12).
